description: VYOMIX is an ambitious team of engineering minds passionate about space exploration, physics, aerospace technology and scientific innovation. We aim to design and develop an interactive, physics-based space mission simulator that combines orbital mechanics, spacecraft engineering, mission optimization and intelligent decision-making. We believe in turning complex scientific concepts into functional solutions. We welcome passionate problem-solvers.
summary: ASTRANOVA is an advanced aerospace engineering simulation platform designed to help engineering students understand rocket design, propulsion, flight dynamics, orbital mechanics and spacecraft systems. Users can assemble launch vehicles and satellites, analyse engineering parameters, control simulated launches, perform orbital manoeuvres and complete progressive space missions. The platform combines interactive 3D environments, mission-control telemetry and engineering calculations to provide practical learning through simulation. Its five mission levels progress from atmospheric launch to lunar landing, encouraging technical problem-solving, system design and mission analysis.
details:
ASTRANOVA – Advanced Aerospace Engineering Simulator

ASTRANOVA is an interactive 3D space exploration and aerospace engineering learning platform designed for engineering students. It allows users to explore spacecraft design, assemble rocket components, understand launch sequences and experience progressive space missions, from atmospheric launch to lunar exploration.

The platform combines a 3D visual environment, mission-based learning, spacecraft assembly and an interactive mission-control interface. Its objective is to make complex aerospace concepts such as propulsion, rocket staging, flight dynamics and orbital mechanics easier to understand through practical visual learning.

Developed using React, TypeScript, Vite and Three.js, ASTRANOVA focuses on interactive design and immersive simulation. Its mission themes are inspired by NASA's Apollo, Artemis, Voyager, James Webb, Perseverance and DART missions.

The project aims to encourage engineering creativity, technical curiosity and interest in space science while making aerospace education more accessible.
